Threats.Description: The route requires a wrapper or pre-start materializer that direct Unity startup can bypass.
More than one mutable input can independently select a generation.
Unity, UPM, or the harness writes bytes classified as immutable authority.
Runtime, Editor, and AutoChess do not resolve to one generation.
A lock file, PackageCache, unpack directory, Bee output, or response file acts as a fallback selector.
The SourceGenerator route needs a different selector or token per assembly.
One or more of Runtime, Editor, and AutoChess do not recompile after the selector changes.
The candidate requires existing active generated source to participate in compilation.
Stale Bee or response-file state determines the final generation.
The forced ActiveGenerationRef versus candidate-selector conflict has more than one Unity consumer.
The forced conflict result depends on cache state or startup order.
A production protected path changes between J0 and J2.
The disposable fixture escapes its owned root or contains a hardlink or reparse point.
Required raw evidence or an identity binding is missing and cannot support a route conclusion.
A bounded probe exceeds its fixed time box; the run is not automatically extended.
